title: France addr_tokens: city and place-name coverage
headline: Top-10 French places cover at most 85.174% of French test rows (1,443,231 of 1,694,445) and only 12 of the top-30 unigrams are places. City is already an unintentional blocking key but only in compound form (keys.py has no bare-address-token key kind), so adding city as a blocking key is a no-op. New defect: 19 ADDR_CANON_FR canonicals are missing from ADDR_GENERIC, leaking 336,623 occurrences (19.866 per 100 rows) into the key vocabulary; and normalize.py does not handle the U+2019 typographic apostrophe, which splits French elisions.
most_important_number: 85.174 occurrences per 100 French rows = 1,443,231 of 1,694,445, an UPPER bound on the top-10 row share
revision_note: A prior draft and sidecar existed. All figures re-derived from the profile. Three errors corrected (bound direction, non-existent bare-city key kind, mixed s1/all-source denominators), one reclassification (r and n are abbreviations, not accent fragments), one arithmetic fix (legacy regions), and one omission added (U+2019).

invariants_verified: sum(len_hist.values()) == by_country.France.rows for all three France slices

unit_caveat.statement: addr_tokens counts token OCCURRENCES, not rows. occurrences/rows is occurrences-per-row and is NOT a percentage of rows; it can exceed 100. Every rate in this deliverable is stated as occurrences per 100 rows.
unit_caveat.reason: build_profile.py:112-127 pools all comma-separated components into one counter; no token-to-row or token-to-component mapping is retained

a_top_places.method: merged counts across s1/s2/s3; a multi-word place uses min over its constituent tokens because the generic component is shared

saint_is_not_a_place_count.reason: saint is simultaneously a commune prefix, a street element (Rue Saint-Martin) and part of Saint-Herblain
saint_is_not_a_place_count.consequence: the naive sum of the 10 head tokens (1,515,562) overstates the top-10 total, so the min-token proxy is used

b_top10_share.bound_direction: UPPER bound on the row share, because occurrences >= rows
b_top10_share.stability: within 0.9 pp across all three sources, so a property of the French data and not of one source's formatting
b_top10_share.cross_check_source: analyse_france.py, row-level, computed from raw data
b_top10_share.cross_check_note: 84.58 <= 85.174, so the upper bound is satisfied and the true row share lies between the two

c_separability.verdict: NOT cleanly separable from the profile; only partially in the pipeline
reasons: the profile destroys component identity: build_profile.py:126-127 splits on comma/semicolon then pools all components into one counter, so component index is discarded

the profile tokeniser shatters accented place names: TOKEN_RE = [a-z0-9]+ (build_profile.py:28) does not strip accents, so Merignac -> m+rignac (rignac 51156 vs merignac 14416, 3.5x) and Lege-Cap-Ferret -> l+ge+cap+ferret (ge 41120 vs lege 11261, 3.6x); merignac and lege are exactly 0 in s1

in the pipeline, normalize.py:322-352 builds city_comps from every digit-free component, so street components are also labelled as cities (verified: '45 Rue de l Eglise, Tourcoing' -> city_comps ['rue de l eglise', 'tourcoing'])
the profile tokenisation is NOT the pipeline tokenisation: normalize.py:317 calls strip_accents(), verified '175 Rue de la Merignac, Merignac' -> ['175','rue','de','la','merignac','merignac']
c_separability.street_words_evidence: rue 728583, avenue 126497, boulevard 38275 all reach canonical forms present in ADDR_GENERIC, which keys.py:39 drops before key generation

new_defect_typographic_apostrophe.status: LIKELY - code defect CONFIRMED, data prevalence UNVERIFIED
new_defect_typographic_apostrophe.cause: _non_alnum.split(c.replace(ASCII_APOSTROPHE, empty)) strips the ASCII apostrophe only; U+2019 is left in place and _non_alnum = [^a-z0-9]+ then treats it as a separator
new_defect_typographic_apostrophe.consequence: the same address yields two different token vectors, and the U+2019 form emits a meaningless 1-char token l

supporting_profile_evidence.note: at least 58,769 l occurrences cannot be explained by Lege alone

new_defect_typographic_apostrophe.french_specific: elision (l', d', qu', n', c', j') is exactly where U+2019 appears
new_defect_typographic_apostrophe.impact: blocking-key impact limited because keys.py:42 drops tokens shorter than 3 chars; the cost lands on the IDF-weighted features path at features.py:120-123

defect1_source_vocabulary_split.residual_explanation: my count omits pas de calais (pas 29032 occ) and loire atlantique spelled whole, both of which are in FR_REGIONS
defect1_source_vocabulary_split.fr_regions_is_not_the_bottleneck: nord, gironde, loire atlantique and pas de calais are all present at normalize.py:244-247; the bottleneck is rows carrying no mappable component

defect2_missing_from_addr_generic.length_filter_note: all 19 are 3+ chars or have zero measured mass (za and zi are 2 chars but never occur), so all 336,623 occurrences are eligible to reach alph
defect2_missing_from_addr_generic.end_to_end_verification: normalize_address('5 Rue des Lilas, Saint-Nazaire') -> toks ['5','rue','des','lilas','saint','nazaire'] -> alph ['nazaire','lilas','saint']
defect2_missing_from_addr_generic.mitigating_factor: alph is sorted longest-first (keys.py:43), so the 3-char leakers are pushed down and only make the cut when the address yields fewer than 9 longer tokens; saint at 5 chars is the one that genuinely competes

defect3_abbreviation_split.reason: ADDR_CANON_FR maps both spellings to the same canonical value, so token identity is preserved
defect3_abbreviation_split.consequence: any s1-tuned French threshold is mis-set for 84.7% of French rows

key_kinds_defined.2: num x addr-token and addr-token x addr-token

d_blocking.non_separability_evidence: for '12 Rue Dunkerque, Lille' the alph is ['dunkerque','lille'] - the street Dunkerque and the city Lille are indistinguishable to the key builder
d_blocking.recommendation_reason: no bare-city key kind exists, and the df caps already drop the city-bearing compound keys, so adding city is a no-op at best

cap_arithmetic_s1_index.governs: the source-1 index only (blocking.py:13,16), so all numerators must be s1-only
cap_arithmetic_s1_index.assumption: uniform spread of house numbers over the city; the profile has no row-level co-occurrence, so this cell size is inferred, not measured

d_blocking.residual_risk: budget dilution rather than collisions: city tokens and the 19 defect-2 leakers compete for the same 9 alph slots, longest-first

gaps: no component/axis field: tokens are pooled across comma-separated components (build_profile.py:126-127), so which component a token came from is unanswerable, including the work order's {axis} framing and the region-before-or-after-city ordering question
no row-level co-occurrence: the (number, city) cell sizes are inferred from marginals under a uniform-spread assumption, not measured
no alph-occupancy histogram: the dilution magnitude of defect 2 is unquantified

no distinct-city count: the vocabulary is truncated at 4000 tokens per source, so the true number of distinct French places is unknown; the 5,960 figure quoted in the work order is not reproducible from this profile
accent folding is a profile artefact: rignac and merignac are the same place under two spellings and the true split is unrecoverable
saint is not separable from a place: it is simultaneously a place prefix, a street element and a commune prefix across its 141,364 occurrences
U+2019 prevalence is unknown: the profile tokeniser discards the apostrophe character, so the elision-splitting defect is confirmed in the code but unquantified in the data

recommendations.action: Add the 19 missing French canonical forms to ADDR_GENERIC in _upstream/src/keys.py: saint, sainte, bis, rte, crs, quai, res, gen, mal, bat, fbg, prof, pres, lieu, lieudit, zone, za, zi, zac
recommendations.expected_effect: Removes 336,623 occurrences (19.866 per 100 French rows) of pure street/building grammar from the key vocabulary and frees alph slots

recommendations.action: Do not tune any French threshold or dictionary on test_source1 alone
recommendations.expected_effect: s1 is 15.31% of French rows and uses a different address convention (regions, 1.5% r-abbreviation) from s2/s3 (departments, ~40% r); avoids mis-calibration for 84.7% of French rows

recommendations.action: Normalise U+2019 and U+02BC to ASCII apostrophe in normalize.py before the strip at line 342, and likewise at line 273 in normalize_name
recommendations.confidence: LIKELY - code defect CONFIRMED, data prevalence UNVERIFIED
recommendations.expected_effect: Removes spurious 1-char tokens from the IDF feature path; blocking-key effect is small because keys.py:42 already drops tokens shorter than 3 chars

recommendations.action: Reconcile the region-resolvability contradiction (2.56% vs 28.90% unresolvable) and add the remaining modern French region names to FR_REGIONS
recommendations.expected_effect: My ceiling is 69.11% and the work order's is 71.10%; the legacy names are not where the gap lives, totalling only 10,000 occurrences = 0.590 per 100 rows

recommendations.action: NO CHANGE - do not add city as a blocking key
recommendations.expected_effect: No bare-city key kind exists and the df caps already drop city-bearing compound keys; recorded to prevent a redundant or harmful later fix

recommendations.action: NO CHANGE - the s1/s2/s3 abbreviation split is not a matching bug; ADDR_CANON_FR collapses both spellings to the same canonical token
recommendations.expected_effect: None; matters for threshold calibration, not token identity

recommendations.action: NO CHANGE - accent handling in the pipeline is correct (strip_accents at normalize.py:317); the m/rignac and l/ge fragmentation is a build_profile.py TOKEN_RE artefact
recommendations.expected_effect: If the profile is rebuilt, TOKEN_RE should strip accents first, but note this would also mask the U+2019 defect, so both profile fixes should be considered together

legacy_region_check.purpose: test whether legacy French region names explain the unresolvable-row gap
legacy_region_check.excluded: aquitaine, because it is part of nouvelle aquitaine and not a legacy region
legacy_region_check.conclusion: legacy names are NOT where the missing ~31% lives; the gap is rows carrying no region or department component at all

corrections_to_prior_draft.correction: occurrences >= rows, so rows outside the top 10 is a LOWER bound (>= 251,214) and inside is an UPPER bound (<= 85.174%)

corrections_to_prior_draft.prior_claim: a bare city key would be dropped outright, 1454x over cap for Bordeaux
corrections_to_prior_draft.correction: keys.py:56-73 emits no singleton-address-token kind; city enters only compound keys, so the cap arithmetic must be redone on compounds

corrections_to_prior_draft.prior_claim: (num, city) = 535.7 per cell = 17.9x the cap, from 518 numbers and 277,474 Bordeaux occurrences
corrections_to_prior_draft.correction: the cap governs the s1 index only; s1 has 373 numeric tokens and 43,634 Bordeaux occurrences, giving 117.0 per cell = 3.9x, and 223 of 373 numbers occur 200 times or fewer

corrections_to_prior_draft.prior_claim: r, n and l are all fragments produced by accent shattering

the U+2019 typographic apostrophe is not handled in normalize.py:342 or :273, splitting l'Eglise into l + eglise

already_checked_dispositions.REFUTED_1_france_postcode_loss: Not re-derived; nothing in this deliverable bears on it. For the record my s1 figures are consistent: dig5 = 1,082 and dig6 = 34 over 259,452 s1 France rows. The top-30 addr list is dominated by house numbers (1 = 8,195 through 17 = 4,277), confirming French addresses carry numbers but not postcodes.
already_checked_dispositions.REFUTED_2_france_region_claim: Re-scoping CONFIRMED with numbers. The famous 100% is a test_source1-only denominator and s1 is 15.31% of French rows. My independent component-level ceiling is 69.11% across all three sources versus the work order's 71.10%; both agree the s1 figure does not generalise. Mechanism identified: s1 writes regions (100.15 occ per 100 rows) while s2/s3 write departments (30.45 and 29.59), and roughly 31% of French rows carry neither. French geography is NOT settled.
